question:
(a) Describe thermionic emission, field emission and photoelectric emission on the basis of the energy supplied to electrons.
(b) Why are metals having low work function preferred for electron emission? Give reason.

options.A:
(a) Thermionic emission is caused by light, field emission by heat, and photoelectric emission by magnetic field.
(b) Low-work-function metals are avoided because electrons escape too easily.
options.B:
(a) Thermionic emission uses heat energy, field emission uses a very strong electric field, and photoelectric emission uses radiation of suitable frequency; in each case electrons must overcome the work function.
(b) Low-work-function metals are preferred because less energy is needed to satisfy $E\geq\phi_0$, so electron emission occurs more readily.
options.C:
(a) All three types are caused by the same heat energy.
(b) Work function has no effect on emission.
options.D:
(a) Field emission is caused by photon absorption and photoelectric emission by electric fields.
(b) Higher-work-function metals emit electrons more easily.
